title: Check yourself: Subagents, their memory, and hooks

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A reviewer subagent's file has no `tools` line. What can it do?

options.text: Read only, because a review of code needs nothing more than reading it
options.says: Ruled out because a reviewer is bounded only when you list `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob`, as the page says: "Bound a subagent by listing its tools."

options.text: Nothing at all, because an empty list gives the subagent no tools to use
options.says: Ruled out because the table says "Omit it and the subagent inherits every tool", which is the opposite of none.

options.text: Use every tool of the session, including editing and running commands
options.says: The page says "Omit it and the subagent inherits every tool", and "a reviewer with no `tools` line can edit files and run commands".

options.text: Use only the tools that the main conversation allows without asking first
options.says: Ruled out because a subagent has "specific tool access, and independent permissions", and an omitted list does not narrow it to the main conversation's pre-approvals.

questions.stem: A hook script is meant to stop `git push`. Which behaviour stops the call?

options.text: Exiting with code 2 with the reason written to standard error
options.says: The page says "Exit 2: Claude Code blocks the action. Write a reason to stderr."

options.text: Printing a warning to standard output and exiting with code 1
options.says: Ruled out because with an exit code of 1 and plain-text output "the action proceeds as a non-blocking error", and a warning does not stop the call.

options.text: Exiting with code 0 after logging the command to a file
options.says: Ruled out because "Exit 0: no objection", and a logging hook "does not weaken a guard hook" and does not block either.

options.text: Exiting with code 3 after writing a reason to standard error
options.says: Ruled out because exit code 3 is an "other exit code", and the page says to "Treat it as a bug in the hook, because it does not stop the call."

questions.stem: A subagent builds notes on a repository, and teammates should receive them through version control. Which `memory` value fits?

options.text: `user`, whose directory sits in each person's home folder
options.says: Ruled out because the `user` scope is for a case where "The agent should remember across all projects", and its directory is under `~/.claude/`, outside the repository.

options.text: `local`, whose directory is kept out of commits
options.says: Ruled out because the `local` scope is for knowledge that is "project-specific and should not be checked in".

options.text: `team`, whose directory is shared by every teammate
options.says: Ruled out because the field takes one of three values, and the page's own example is flagged: "memory must be user, project or local".

options.text: `project`, whose directory is committed alongside the sources
options.says: The table says the `project` scope, at `.claude/agent-memory/<name>/`, is for knowledge that is "shareable via version control".
